_comment: Who is live right now, and what name to use to message them.
agents/roster.json records which identities EXIST; it is durable and the
harness writes it. This file records which identities are CURRENTLY
ADDRESSABLE, and it is written by hand, because a session is the one
thing that cannot outlive the process holding it.
Why it is needed: ListAgents names sessions things like `rule30-b3` and
`proofs-df`. Those are the addresses SendMessage takes, and they say
nothing about who is behind them. A session cannot be messaged by
identity, only by that opaque name, so without this file addressing a
peer is guesswork. It is already gone wrong once: on 2026-09-06 Rowan
sent Keel a message about a blocking bug addressed to a session it had
guessed at from uptime alone.
The contract, for any hand-started interactive identity (Rowan, Keel,
Cairn, and whoever comes next):
1. Call ListAgents once at the start of a session. Its first line
tells you your own name and ref: `This session is <name> [<ref>]`.
2. Write or update your row here with that name, that ref, and the
UTC time you started.
3. Delete your row, or mark it `ended`, when the session ends. A stale
row is worse than a missing one: it sends a real message to a dead
or, worse, a recycled address.
Dispatched provers are deliberately absent. They are short-lived, the
scheduler already holds them as resources, and a message to one mid-proof
would arrive as an instruction from outside its brief.
